judged_text: In sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, but all nine callers treat the return value as the provider-specific response shape they had before. Google crashes with TypeError reading access_token of undefined (res?.data on a Response), zoho-bigin and zohocrm crash reading .data.error of undefined, hubspot assigns the Response to a HubspotToken so expires_in is undefined and the subsequent credential update persists a key that has lost the real tokens, and lark/zoom/webex/office365video feed the sync body to handlers expecting provider error shapes — enabling the sync env vars breaks or corrupts every integrated app at once rather than only routing refreshes through the endpoint.

adjudication.rationale:
In sharing mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch(...)` `Response` object from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (no `.json()` / no provider-shaped object). Multiple callers still use the pre-existing provider-specific/axios shapes:
- GoogleCalendarService does `const token = res?.data;` and then reads `token.access_token`/`token.expiry_date`, which will be `undefined` on a `Response`, causing a crash.
- Hubspot assigns the return to `HubspotToken` and then uses it as token data; in sharing mode that will be a `Response`, not the expected object.
- Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM expect axios responses (`tokenInfo.data.error`, `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`), which will fail if a `Response` is returned.
So enabling the new sync env vars would break these integrations as described.
